title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF OBLIGATORY FIREFIGHTING UNIT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to provide for matters mandated by the Act on the Establishment of Obligatory Firefighting Unit and other matters necessary for the enforcement thereof. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>

Article 2 (Definitions) (1) "Appointment" in this Decree means new recruitment, transference, promotion, ex officio dismissal, ipso facto retirement, leave of absence, reinstatement, and retirement.
  (2) "Fire service agency prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 1 of the Act on the Establishment of Obligatory Firefighting Unit (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the National Fire Agency, the Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, and Special Self-Governing Province, the National Fire Service Academy, the National 119 Rescue Headquarters, a local fire service academy, fire station, 119 special response unit, and firefighting experience center (hereinafter referred to as "fire service agencies"). <Amended on May 24, 2004; Jun. 23, 2006; Dec. 3, 2008; Jan. 28, 2011; Sep. 17, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; Dec. 22, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017; Oct. 14, 2021; Jun. 23, 2026>
  (3) "Superior" in Article 10 of the Act and this Decree means the head of a fire service agency, fire officials, and obligatory firefighters of a higher rank who have the authority to command and supervise the duties of an obligatory firefighting unit.
  (4) "Commander" in Article 11 of the Act and this Decree means the head of a fire service agency to which an obligatory firefighter belongs.

CHAPTER II APPOINTMENT

Article 3 (Authority to appoint) (1) An obligatory firefighter shall be appointed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency from among those who have been seconded pursuant to Article 25(1) of the Military Service Act. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Jun. 23, 2006; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may delegate all or part of his or her authority to appoint under paragraph (1) to the head of the Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, Special Self-Governing Province, the National Fire Service Academy, the Central 119 Rescue Headquarters, local fire service academy, fire station, 119 special response unit, or firefighting experience center (hereinafter referred to as "affiliated agencies, etc."). <Amended on May 24, 2004; Dec. 3, 2008; Jan. 28, 2011; Sep. 17, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; Dec. 22, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017; Oct. 14, 2021; Jun. 23, 2026>
  (3) Where the head of an affiliated agency, etc. intends to transfer an obligatory firefighter to a fire service agency of another Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province, he or she shall obtain approval from the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency in advance; provided, a transfer of an obligatory firefighter between fire stations within the same Special Metropolitan City, Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province shall require approval from the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Integrated Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as the "Mayor/Do Governor"). <Amended on May 29, 2003; May 24, 2004; Dec. 3, 2008; Nov. 19, 2014; Dec. 22, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017; Jun. 23, 2026>

Article 4 (Selection of persons to be appointed to obligatory firefighters and conducting selection examination) (1) When the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency intends to recommend persons scheduled to be appointed as obligatory firefighters to the Minister of National Defense pursuant to Article 3(2) of the Act, he or she shall conduct an open competitive selection examination for persons scheduled to be appointed as obligatory firefighters (hereinafter referred to as "selection examination for obligatory firefighters") after receiving support from among persons who are in the preliminary military service or supplementary service of at least 18 years of age, and then select such persons. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Nov. 29, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters under paragraph (1) shall be conducted by a physical examination and an interview: provided, if deemed necessary by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, a multiple-choice written examination may be added. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) Notwithstanding the proviso to paragraph (2), when it is intended to select a person who holds a certificate of qualification for performing special duties, such as computerization, driving, hazardous substances, firefighting equipment, fire inspection assistance, or emergency medical service assistance, a practical examination may be conducted in lieu of a written multiple-choice examination.
  (4) The examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall be conducted sequentially according to the steps classified as follows, but no person who has failed to pass the examination in the preceding steps shall apply for the examination in the following steps: <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. Primary examination: Physical examination;
  2. Secondary examination (limited to cases where the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency deems it necessary pursuant to the proviso to paragraph (2) or paragraph (3)): Multiple-choice written examination or practical examination;
  3. Tertiary examination: Oral examination.
  (5) Where the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency deems it necessary to conduct an examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters in each stage pursuant to paragraph (4), he or she may conduct the following stage of the examination before a passing decision of the previous stage of the examination. <Newly Inserted on May. 29, 2003; May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 5 (Determination of success in examination and preparation of list of successful applicants) (1) The determination of success in each step of examinations for the selection of obligatory firefighters shall be made in accordance with each of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on May 29, 2003>
  1. In cases of a primary examination, a decision shall be made to allow an applicant pass or fail the examination after determining whether the applicant meets the standards for a physical examination under Article 7;
  2. In cases of a secondary examination, success shall be determined within the limit of 120% of the number of persons to be selected in the order of high scorers in the written examination or practical examination in consideration of the number of persons who are to fail in the tertiary examination: provided, that where there are persons who obtain the same scores in excess of the number of persons to be selected in the secondary examination, all of them shall be deemed successful candidates, notwithstanding the number of persons to be selected;
  3. In cases of a tertiary examination, success shall be determined by adding a small number of candidates after considering those who fail to pass the physical examination for enlistment and those who have returned home due to illness or mental or physical disability, and in the order of high scorers in the oral examination results.
  (2) The Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall prepare a list of applicants according to the list of applicants for the examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters in attached Form 1 with respect to those who apply for the examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters under Article 4, and shall record the results of each step of examinations in the list. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 6 (Recommendation of persons to be appointed to obligatory firefighters) (1) When the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency intends to recommend a person to be appointed as an obligatory firefighter to the Minister of National Defense pursuant to Article 3(2) of the Act, he or she shall recommend a person determined to be the final successful candidate for the examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters pursuant to Article 5. In such cases, the order of priority of persons who pass the examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters shall be based on the order of seniority. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The recommendation referred to in paragraph (1) shall be made based on the recommendation list of candidates for appointment of obligatory firefighters in attached Form 2, and the recommendation shall be made not later than 60 days before the date of enlistment of prospective obligatory firefighters. <Amended on Nov. 29, 2016>

Article 7 (Methods and standards for physical examination and oral examination) (1) A physical examination shall be conducted based on a physical examination report issued by the head of a national or public hospital or general hospital, but where the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency deems it necessary, he or she may directly examine whether an applicant meets the standards for physical examination. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The standards for the physical examination of obligatory firefighters under paragraph (1) shall be as specified in attached Table 1. <Amended on Oct. 17, 2017>
  (3) The oral examination shall be conducted by examining the application documents submitted pursuant to Article 9 and conducting an aptitude test, and the methods and criteria therefor shall be determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 8 (Subjects, methods, and level of questions in written examinations) (1) Where a written examination is conducted pursuant to the proviso to Article 4(2), the subjects shall be Korean language, Korean history, and general common sense, and matters necessary for conducting the written examination, such as the method of examination and the number of questions prepared for each subject, shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (2) The questions for a written examination under paragraph (1) shall be at the level of a high school graduate: provided, if deemed necessary by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, the level of the examination may be set differently. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 9 (Application documents) (1) A person who intends to apply for an examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters shall submit an application form for the examination for the selection of obligatory firefighters in attached Form 3 (including an application in electronic form) to the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, along with the following documents. <Amended on Oct. 22, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; Nov. 29, 2016; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. In cases of a person who has undergone a draft physical examination under Article 11(1) of the Military Service Act: One copy of a written notice of the results of the draft physical examination;
  2. In cases of a person who has undergone a draft physical examination under Article 11(1) of the Military Service Act;
  a. A copy of a physical examination report issued by the head of a national or public hospital or general hospital;
  b. A copy of the academic background certificate of the last school.
  (2) Upon receipt of an application for application under paragraph (1), the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall verify the following administrative information by sharing administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act: provided, that where an applicant does not consent to verification, the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall require the applicant to attach the relevant documents (in cases falling under subparagraph 2, a copy of his resident registration certificate may be substituted by a copy of his resident registration certificate), respectively. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 2, 2010; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. A certificate of military register;
  2. A certified copy of resident registration card.

Article 10 (Date of appointment) The date of new employment and retirement of an obligatory firefighter shall be the same date as the date of secondment and discharge from military service (when the period of secondment is extended pursuant to Article 25(3) of the Military Service Act, the expiration of the extended period of secondment) of an obligatory firefighter under the Military Service Act, respectively. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006; Dec. 7, 2009>

Article 11 (Career competition employment test) The Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency or a Mayor/Do Governor to whom the authority to appoint firefighting officials has been delegated pursuant to Article 3(1) and (5) 1 and 3 of the Decree on the Appointment of Firefighting Officials may employ obligatory firefighting officials who have completed prescribed service as firefighting officials through a career competition employment test under Article 7(2)3 of the Firefighting Officials Act. <Amended on Aug. 13, 2024>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Mar. 10, 2020]

Article 12 (Education and training) (1) Education and training under Article 4-2(1) of the Act shall be classified into education and training on practical firefighting, education and training on health and safety, education and training on health and safety, and troop information and education under Article 4-2(1) of the Act.
  (2) The contents, cycles, hours, and methods of education and training under paragraph (1) shall be as specified in attached Table 2.
  (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the implementation of education and training shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 17, 2017]

Article 13 (Establishment of operating committee of obligatory firefighting unit) (1) An operating committee of an obligatory firefighting unit (hereinafter referred to as the "operating committee") shall be established under the jurisdiction of the head of a fire service agency to examine the order of candidates for promotion and other matters necessary for the operation of an obligatory firefighting unit under Article 15(4).
  (2) An operating committee shall be comprised of not less than 5 but not more than 7 members, including a chairperson.
  (3) The head of the competent division in charge of the relevant fire service agency shall be the chairperson, and the members shall be appointed by the head of the fire service agency from among firefighting officials of fire commander or higher.
  (4) The operating committee shall pass resolutions with the consent of a majority of all incumbent members.
  (5) Detailed matters necessary for the operation of the operating committee shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 14 (Ranks of obligatory firefighters) (1) The ranks of obligatory firefighters shall be classified into private fireman, private first class fireman, corporal fireman, sergeant fireman, and special fireman.
  (2) The starting rank of an obligatory firefighter shall be private fireman.

Article 15 (Promotion of obligatory firefighters) (1) An obligatory firefighter shall be promoted by one rank from among those whose minimum service period required for promotion has elapsed shall be promoted by one rank: provided, that the promotion to special fireman shall be limited to those who have completed the educational course prescribed by the Army Military Major Academy or the Central Fire-Fighting Academy after having been selected as a member of the squad leadership from among sergeant firemen. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) The minimum service period required for promotion under paragraph (1) shall be as follows: provided, that the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may shorten the minimum service period for promotion with the consent of the Minister of National Defense, if a war or an incident occurs or if deemed necessary to fill a vacancy: <Amended on Dec. 28, 2012; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Aug. 27, 2019>
  1. Promotion to private first class fireman: 2 months from the date of enlistment;
  2. Promotion to corporal fireman: 6 months as private first class fireman;
  3. Promotion to sergeant fireman: 6 months as corporal fireman.
  (3) The following periods shall not be included in the minimum service period under paragraph (2):
  1. Period of leave of absence;
  2. The period from the date of escaping from military service to the date immediately preceding the date of return to military service or arrest;
  3. The period during which a person is hospitalized for reasons other than his duties;
  4. The period during which a disciplinary action is taken.
  (4) The appointing authority shall prepare a list of candidates for promotion with respect to persons eligible for promotion, as prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, following examination by the operating committee. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (5) The appointment of a promotion shall be made in the order of precedence according to the vacancy from among those listed on the list of candidates for promotion under paragraph (4), and the date of appointment announcement shall be the first day of each month.

Article 16 (Restriction on promotion) An obligatory firefighter who falls under any of the following subparagraphs shall not be promoted:
  1. A person who is on leave of absence, absent from work, or undergoing disciplinary action;
  2. A person in whose case the following periods have not elapsed since the date on which the disciplinary action terminated:
  a. 3 months in the case of a military jail;
  b. 2 months in the case of probation;
  c. 1 month in the case of a reprimand.

Article 17 (Special promotion) (1) Notwithstanding Articles 15 and 16, an obligatory firefighter who falls under any of the following subparagraphs may be specially promoted by one rank:
  1. A person who has rendered distinguished service, exemplary to all the members of the brigade in firefighting activities such as fire extinguishment, rescue, and first-aid services;
  2. A person who has rendered distinguished service, exemplary to all members by taking life and completing his duties in a large-scale disaster or accident;
  3. A person who has rendered distinguished service in preventing disasters and accidents such as fires, or in suppressing and coping with disasters and accidents;
  4. A person who died on duty.
  (2) When the appointment authority intends to specially promote a person under paragraph (1), he shall undergo an examination by the operating committee on the merits.
  (3) The procedure and methods for the examination of merits under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 18 (Retirement and withholding of retirement) (1) Where the Minister of National Defense has notified the scheduled date of discharge from secondment pursuant to Article 25(5) and (7) of the Military Service Act, the appointing authority (referring to the head of a firefighting agency delegated where the authority to appoint is delegated pursuant to Article 3(2); hereinafter the same shall apply) shall issue a retirement order to the relevant obligatory firefighter on the same date, if the Minister of National Defense has notified the scheduled date of discharge from secondment pursuant to Article 25(5) and (7) of the Military Service Act. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006; Dec. 7, 2009; Nov. 10, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (1), where an obligatory firefighter falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the appointing authority shall not issue a retirement order. In such cases, the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall request the Minister of National Defense to withhold the cancellation of secondment to the relevant obligatory firefighter. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. Where he deserts his military service or disappears;
  2. When he is subject to a disposition of leave of absence or detention in a guardhouse;
  3. Where he is hospitalized for medical treatment due to an injury in the line of duty, illness, or mental or physical disorder; provided, that this shall not apply where a doctor's decision to discontinue medical treatment is made, or where a person who has suffered a medical injury desires to retire from office.

CHAPTER III SERVICE

Article 19 (Oath) An obligatory firefighter shall take the following oath to the head of a fire service agency at the time of his appointment:
  "I take a solemn oath that I shall be fully loyal to the State, perform my duties as a firefighting agent with all my heart and mind, observe laws and regulations, obey orders of my superiors, and faithfully perform the duties and duties entrusted to me with prudence and courage."

Article 20 (Duties) (1) The duties of obligatory firefighters shall be as follows: <Amended on May. 29, 2003; Jun. 30, 2006; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Assistance in field activities for fires, etc.:
  a. Assistance in the suppression of disasters such as the maintenance of order at the scene of a disaster or an accident such as fire, and support in rescue and first-aid activities;
  b. Securing fire extinguishing water supply systems;
  c. Assistant to on-site commander;
  d. Assistance in situation management;
  e. Other support for matters necessary for on-site activities.
  2. Support for fire service administration:
  a. Assistance in fire service administration such as receipt and delivery of documents;
  b. Assistance in telecommunications and computerization;
  c. Assistance in in-house service at 119 safety center;
  d. Support for maintenance and management of fire extinguishing water supply systems;
  e. Support for fire patrol and preventive operations;
  f. Support for driving vehicles.
  3. Expenses of fire agencies and stations.
  (2) In performing the duties prescribed in paragraph (1), an obligatory firefighter shall comply with the service rules prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency and faithfully perform his duties. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 21 (Obligatory firefighter‘s barrack life and permission for outing) (1) An obligatory firefighter shall live in a barrack.
  (2) The head of a fire service agency may permit an obligatory firefighter to go out, stay out, or visit, as prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 22 (Leave) (1) Leaves of an obligatory firefighter shall be classified into annual leave, official leave, petition leave, compensation leave, compensation leave, and reward leave.
  (2) An obligatory firefighter may take annual leave of up to 25 days a year by dividing the leave once or two times or more.
  (3) Official leave shall be granted for a necessary period when falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
  1. When he is summoned to a court in connection with his official duties;
  2. When he participates in voting in accordance with the provisions of Acts;
  3. Where he is unable to work due to an injury or disease attributable to his official duty.
  (4) Leave on application shall be permitted in accordance with the following standards:
  1. Within 2 months a year, if a person needs to take a leave of absence due to his own injury or illness;
  2. Within 20 days a year, if it is necessary to provide nursing care for the principal due to an injury or disease of a lineal family member, etc.;
  3. Within 14 days per year upon the principal‘s marriage or death of his lineal family members.
  (5) Compassionate leave shall be permitted for a specified period of not more than 7 days when the person becomes very fatigued due to training, patrol, or other special duties.
  (6) Article 9 of the Firefighting Officials Service Regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to a leave of reward. <Amended on Mar. 10, 2020>

Article 23 (Uniforms) Matters necessary for the types, forms of making, standards, and wearing of uniforms for obligatory firefighters shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 24 (Personnel management for persons who deserts his post) (1) An obligatory firefighter who has deserted his post fails to return to his unit without good cause shall be managed as a deserter from the date of desertion from service, and as an expunged deserter unless he returns within 15 days.
  (2) Where a person managed as a deserter or as an expunged deserter returns or is arrested, disciplinary action shall be taken against him or a criminal complaint shall be filed with the competent police station, depending on cases.
  (3) A person managed as an expunged deserter pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be excluded from the current members of the auxiliary police companies, and if he returns or is arrested, measures shall be taken to return him to service without delay.

CHAPTER IV GUARANTEE OF STATUS

Article 25 (Prohibition of measures of status against will) No obligatory firefighter shall be retired, dismissed, or suspended from office against his will, unless he is subject to any cause prescribed by the Act or this Decree.

Article 26 (Ipso facto retirement) When an obligatory firefighter falls under any of the following subparagraphs while in service, he shall retire ipso facto. <Amended on Oct. 17, 2017; Dec. 3, 2019>
  1. When he has lost the nationality of the Republic of Korea;
  2. When he becomes a person under adult guardianship;
  3. Deleted; <Jun. 23, 2006>
  4. When he is sentenced to imprisonment with or without labor for at least 1 year and 6 months.

Article 27 (Ex officio dismissal) (1) Where an obligatory firefighter falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the appointing authority may dismiss him ex officio:
  1. Where he is unable to perform his duties due to a physical or mental disorder;
  2. Where a person who takes a leave of absence due to a reason falling under Article 28(1)1 or 5 fails to perform his duties even after the period of such leave of absence expires;
  3. Where a person who takes a leave of absence for reasons falling under Article 28(1)2 through 4 is alive or dead unknown until the expiration of the period of such leave of absence;
  4. Where a person who has been sentenced to imprisonment with or without labor (excluding a person falling under subparagraph 4 of Article 26) and is deemed unfit to be qualified as an obligatory firefighter.
  (2) Where an appointing authority dismisses an obligatory firefighter ex officio pursuant to paragraph (1), he shall verify a medical certificate issued by the head of the Armed Forces Capital Hospital or the head of a national or public hospital if he falls under subparagraph 1 or 2 of the same paragraph; and where he falls under subparagraph 4 of the same paragraph, he shall undergo an examination by the operating committee: provided, that where he falls under paragraph (1)1 or 2 and where the determination of a physical grade under Article 12(1) of the Military Service Act finds that he does not fall under Grade V or VI or where he falls under paragraph (1)4, the appointing authority shall decide on ex officio dismissal following a request for release from secondment under Article 27-2. <Amended on Nov. 10, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 2, 2016]

Article 27-2 (Request for cancellation of secondment) (1) Where an obligatory firefighter falls under any of the following cases, the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may request the Minister of National Defense to cancel secondment:
  1. Where an obligatory firefighter falls under Article 27(1)1 or 2 and the determination of his physical grade under Article 12(1) of the Military Service Act finds that he does not fall under Grade V or VI;
  2. Where he falls under Article 27(1)4.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for cancellation of secondment pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall deal with the request pursuant to Article 65(1) and (11) of the Military Service Act and notify the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency of the results thereof.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020]

Article 28 (Leave of absence) (1) Where an obligatory firefighter falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the appointing authority shall order him to take a leave of absence:
  1. Where he is unable to perform his duties due to a disease or mental or physical disorder caused by any cause other than official duties;
  2. Where it is unclear if he is alive or dead during firefighting activities at the scene of a disaster such as extinguishing a fire;
  3. Where whether he is alive or dead is unknown due to a war, incident, natural disaster, or accident of aircraft, ship, etc.;
  4. Where whether he is alive or dead for reasons other than those referred to in subparagraphs 2 and 3;
  5. Where a person who has taken a leave of absence due to an injury or disease needs continuous medical treatment even after the period of leave expires;
  6. Where he is arrested or prosecuted for a criminal case or is subject to imprisonment with or without labor for less than one year and six months.
  (2) The period of leave of absence referred to in paragraph (1)1 and 5 shall be within six months; the period of leave of absence in paragraph (1)2 and 3 within three years; the period of leave in paragraph (1)4 within one year; and that in paragraph (1)6 shall be within the period of continuation of the relevant case, or until the period during which the execution of the sentence is terminated or the non-execution of the sentence is confirmed.
  (3) Necessary matters concerning the medical treatment and the confirmation of the degree of recovery of persons who have taken leave of absence pursuant to paragraph (1)1 shall be prescribed by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 29 (Effect of leave of absence) (1) An obligatory firefighter on a leave of absence shall retain his status but shall not engage in his duties.
  (2) The appointing authority shall, without delay, order the reinstatement of an obligatory firefighter when the grounds for a leave of absence cease to exist during the period of such leave.
  (3) An obligatory firefighter whose period of leave of absence has expired shall be reinstated ipso facto: provided, that this shall not apply to cases falling under Article 28(1)2 through 4 and 6.

Article 30 (Non-inclusion of period of secondment in period of leave of absence) (1) The following periods shall not be included in the secondment service period of an obligatory firefighter: provided, that where a person who has taken leave of absence for reasons falling under Article 28(1)6 is adjudged not guilty, or receives a judgment or decision of non-transfer, non-prosecution, acquittal, or dismissal of public prosecution due to any cause not attributable to the person, the period of leave of absence as a result shall be included in the secondment service period: <Amended on Dec. 29, 2020>
  1. Period of leave of absence;
  2. The period from the date of escaping from military service to the date immediately preceding the date of return to military service or arrest;
  3. Period of execution of detention in a guardhouse.
  (2) In any of the following cases, the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall notify the Minister of National Defense of his personal information and the period of leave of absence, the period of desertion from service, or the period of execution of detention in a guardhouse. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  1. When a person on a leave of absence has been reinstated;
  2. When a person who has deserted his service has been returned to military service or has been arrested;
  3. When the execution of detention in a guardhouse of a person subject to such disposition is terminated.

Article 30-2 (Composition and operation of common review committee on casualties in the line of duty) (1) A common review committee on casualties in the line of duty (hereinafter referred to as "common review committee on casualties") shall be established in a firefighting agency to examine matters concerning deaths or injuries that occur while an obligatory firefighter performs his duties.
  (2) A common review committee on casualties shall be comprised of not less than 5 but not more than 7 members, including a chairperson.
  (3) The chairperson of the common review committee on casualties shall be elected by and from among its members.
  (4) The chairperson of the common review committee on casualties shall represent the general committee for examination and exercise overall control of its affairs.
  (5) Where the chairperson of the common review committee on casualties is unable to perform his duties due to any unavoidable cause, a member of the committee designated in advance by its chairperson shall act on behalf of the chairperson.
  (6) The members of the common review committee on casualties shall be appointed or commissioned by the head of a fire service agency from among the following persons, taking into consideration gender equality; in such cases, members who are not public officials shall constitute a majority of the members:
  1. Fire officials whose rank is higher than that of fire lieutenant;
  2. Persons with extensive knowledge of and experience in related fields.
  (7) The term of office of the members of a common review committee on casualties shall be 2 years and may be consecutively renewed only once.
  (8) The chairperson of a common review committee on casualties shall convene and preside over meetings of the committee.
  (9) A majority of the members of the common review committee on casualties shall constitute a quorum and any decision thereof shall require the concurring vote of a majority of those present.
  (10) The head of a fire service agency shall, without delay, notify the applicant of a written decision, including the following matters, when the review by the common review committee on casualties committee is completed:
  1. Results of the review and reasons therefor;
  2. The period for filing a petition for re-review pursuant to Article 30-4(3).
  (11) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (10), detailed matters necessary for the operation, etc. of a common review committee shall be determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020]

Article 30-3 (Composition and operation of central review committee on casualties in the line of duty) (1) In order to review matters concerning the death or injury of obligatory firefighters in the course of performing their duties pursuant to Article 30-4(1) and (2), the National Fire Agency shall establish a Central Review Committee on Casualties (hereinafter referred to as the "Central Review Committee").
  (2) The central review committee shall be comprised of not more than 20 members, including a chairperson.
  (3) Meetings of the central review committee shall be comprised of the chairperson and six members designated by the chairperson for each meeting. In such cases, members who are not public officials shall constitute a majority of the members of the central review committee.
  (4) Article 30-2(3) through (11) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the composition and operation of the central review committee. In such cases, "common review committee" shall be deemed "central review committee", "the head of a firefighting agency" as "the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency", and "review" as "re-review", respectively.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020]

Article 30-4 (Re-review of central review committee) (1) In any of the following cases, the central review committee shall re-review the matters reviewed by a common review committee:
  1. Where the relevant party files a request for re-review;
  2. Where the heir or legal representative of the party requests a re-review (limited to where the party is dead, where the party is in a mental or physical disability or where it is unclear whether he is alive or dead);
  3. Where the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission or the National Human Rights Commission of Korea makes a recommendation or decision different from the review by a common review committee.
  (2) Where the central review committee has conducted re-review pursuant to paragraph (1), the relevant party, inheritors, or legal representatives of the party (hereafter in Article 30-5 referred to as "the party, etc.") may request the central review committee to conduct re-review on the same matter only once.
  (3) A request for re-review under paragraph (1)1 and 2 and (2) shall be made within 90 days from the date on which a written decision on the relevant review or re-review is notified, respectively.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020]

Article 30-5 (Exclusion, challenge, or recusal of members) (1) Any member of the central review committee or common review committee (hereinafter referred to as "review committee on casualties in the line of duty") who falls under any of the following shall be excluded from deliberation and resolution of the agenda:
  1. Where the member or his or her current or former spouse is a party, etc. to the relevant agenda item or is a joint holder of any right with the party, etc. to the relevant agenda item;
  2. Where a member is or was a relative of a party, etc. to the relevant agenda item;
  3. Where a member has provided advice, conducted research, provided services (including subcontracting), performed appraisals, or conducted inspections with respect to the relevant agenda;
  4. Where the member is or was involved in the relevant agenda item as an agent of a party, etc.
  (2) If any ground exists for which it would be impracticable to expect the impartial deliberation of any member of a review committee on casualties in the line of duty, a party to the relevant agenda may request the committee to challenge the member, and the committee shall make a decision on such request by resolution. In such cases, the member subject to such request for challenge shall not participate in the relevant resolution.
  (3) Any member who falls under any ground for disqualification referred to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall notify a review committee on casualties in the line of duty of such fact and voluntarily refrain from deliberations and decisions on the relevant agenda item.
  (4) Where a member of a review committee on casualties in the line of duty fails to refrain despite falling under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the appointing authority or commissioning authority may dismiss or decommission the relevant member.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020]

CHAPTER V DISCIPLINARY ACTION

Article 31 (Jurisdiction over disciplinary cases) Disciplinary cases against obligatory firefighters shall be deliberated on and resolved by the firefighting officials' disciplinary committee established in the agency to which the obligatory firefighting unit belongs (hereinafter referred to as the "disciplinary committee"). <Amended on Dec. 3, 2008>

Article 32 (Request for disciplinary decision) (1) When the head of a fire service agency deems that an obligatory firefighter under his or her jurisdiction falls under any of the following subparagraphs, he or she shall request the competent disciplinary committee to pass a resolution on disciplinary action. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2008>
  1. When an obligatory firefighter has violated the provisions of the Act or this Decree;
  2. When an obligatory firefighter violates any of his official duties or neglects his duties;
  3. When an obligatory firefighter commits an act degrading his dignity;
  4. When an obligatory firefighter fails to obey an order of his superior;
  5. When an obligatory firefighter deserts his place of service or fails to return to military service without good cause;
  6. When an obligatory firefighter has violated other service rules.
  (2) A request for a resolution on disciplinary action under paragraph (1) shall be made after a thorough investigation of the facts constituting the grounds for the disciplinary action. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2008>

Article 33 (Relationship to investigations by board of audit and inspection) (1) With respect to a case under investigation by the Board of Audit and Inspection, any request for a resolution on disciplinary action or any disciplinary procedures shall not be proceeded from the date on which he is notified of the commencement of an investigation under paragraph (3).
  (2) With respect to a case under investigation by the prosecution, the police, or any other investigative agency, any request for a resolution on disciplinary action or any disciplinary procedures may not be proceeded from the date on which he is notified of the commencement of an investigation under paragraph (3).
  (3) When the Board of Audit and Inspection, the prosecution, the police, or any other investigative agency commences or terminates an inspection or investigation into an obligatory firefighter, it shall notify the head of the agency to which the obligatory firefighter belongs of such fact within 10 days.

Article 34 (Notification of grounds for disciplinary actions) (1) Where the head of a fire service agency deems that an obligatory firefighter who does not belong to the fire service agency falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 32(1), he or she shall notify the head of the relevant fire service agency of such fact specifying sufficient grounds to prove it.
  (2) The head of a fire service agency in receipt of notification under paragraph (1) shall request the competent disciplinary committee to pass a resolution on disciplinary action within 10 days from the date of receipt of such notification, unless there is a reasonable ground for notification. <Amended on Dec. 3, 2008>

Article 35 (Period for requesting resolution on disciplinary action) (1) A request for a resolution on disciplinary action shall not be made after 2 years (3 years in cases of receiving money, valuables, entertainment, or embezzlement or misappropriation of public funds) have elapsed from the date on which the grounds for disciplinary action occurred.
  (2) Where the period referred to in paragraph (1) has elapsed or the remaining period thereof is less than one month because the disciplinary procedures are not proceeded pursuant to Article 33(1) and (2), the period under paragraph (1) shall be deemed to expire on the date on which one month has elapsed from the date on which the completion of a survey or an investigation under Article 33(3) is notified.
  (3) When an appeals review committee or a court has made a decision or judgment to nullify or revoke a disciplinary action on the grounds of defects in the composition of a disciplinary committee, a resolution on disciplinary action, or other procedural defects or excessive disciplinary punishment, it may request another disciplinary resolution within 3 months from the date on which such decision or judgment becomes final and conclusive, even if the period under paragraph (1) has elapsed or the remaining period is less than 3 months.

Article 36 (Provisions applicable mutatis mutandis) The provisions of Articles 11 through 19 and 20 of the Decree on Disciplinary Action against Firefighting Officials shall apply mutatis mutandis to disciplinary action against obligatory firefighters. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>

CHAPTER VI APPEALS

Article 37 (Filing of appeals) Where an obligatory firefighter intends to file an appeal pursuant to Article 6 of the Act, he or she shall submit to the disciplinary committee established in the agency to which the relevant obligatory firefighting unit belongs, a written application for reviewing an appeal stating the following matters (hereinafter referred to as "application") within 15 days from the date he or she receives a written explanatory statement on the grounds for disciplinary action or a notice of personnel appointment, along with a copy of the written explanatory statement on the grounds for disciplinary action or a notice of personnel appointment: <Amended on Dec. 3, 2008>
  1. Name, address, and date of birth;
  2. Name and rank of the institution to which he belongs;
  3. The appellee (referring to the person authorized to execute the relevant disciplinary action; hereinafter the same shall apply);
  4. Purport of the appeal;
  5. Grounds for the appeal and the method of substantiating it;
  6. Where an appeal review is requested after the lapse of the period for filing an appeal stated in the explanatory note on the grounds for disciplinary action or the notice of personnel appointment due to delay in receipt of the explanatory note on the grounds for disciplinary action or the notice of personnel appointment, materials substantiating the delay in receipt thereof.

Article 38 (Deadline for review of appeals) The disciplinary committee shall make a decision on the appeal within 20 days from the date of receipt of the appeal: provided, that where it is deemed inevitable, the period may be extended by a resolution of the disciplinary committee by fixing a period not exceeding 10 days.

Article 39 (Decision on appeals cases) (1) The appeals case shall be decided by a majority of the incumbent members of the competent disciplinary committee.
  (2) In examining an appeal case, the disciplinary committee shall not make a decision to impose a disciplinary action heavier than that imposed in the original disciplinary action.

Article 40 (Forwarding of written decision) A written decision on appeals review shall be prepared with an authentic copy thereof and shall be forwarded to each appellant without delay.

Article 41 (Effect of written decision) The decision of the disciplinary committee shall bind the person against whom a petition is filed.

Article 42 (Provisions applicable mutatis mutandis) The provisions of Articles 3 through 15 and 21 of the Regulations on Procedures for Appeal shall apply mutatis mutandis to appeals against obligatory firefighters. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>

CHAPTER VII COMPENSATION

Article 43 (Death benefits) (1) Where an obligatory firefighter is killed in the line of duty such as fire extinguishment, pursuant to Article 7 of the Act (including deaths from injury; hereinafter the same shall apply), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay death benefits to his bereaved family members. In such cases, Article 39(2) of the Military Accident Compensation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the amount of death benefits to be paid to the obligatory firefighter. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Apr. 11, 2023>
  (2) Articles 5 and 13 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to the scope and order of bereaved families who are entitled to receive death benefits under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 22, 2013]

Article 44 (Disability benefits) Where an obligatory firefighter who has retired after having been injured in the line of duty such as fire extinguishment, etc. pursuant to Article 7 of the Act, is assigned a disability rating under Article 6-4 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay disability benefits according to the following classification. <Amended on Nov. 10, 2020; Apr. 11, 2023>
  1. Injured persons assigned Disability Rating 1: An amount calculated according to the following formula:
  <img src="http://www.law.go.kr/flDownload.do?flSeq=81548599" alt="img81548599" .>
  (Average base monthly income of all public officials × 419) 78;
  ( ──────────────────────────────── ) × ───
  (1,000 ) 10
  </img>
  2. Injured persons assigned Disability Ratings 2 to 5: An amount calculated according to the following formula:
  <img src="http://www.law.go.kr/flDownload.do?flSeq=81548599" alt="img81548599" .>
  (Average base monthly income of all public officials × 419) × 52;
  ( ──────────────────────────────── ) × ───
  (1,000 ) 10
  </img>
  3. Injured persons assigned Disability Rating 6 or 7: An amount calculated according to the following formula:
  <img src="http://www.law.go.kr/flDownload.do?flSeq=81548607" alt="img81548607" .>

  ( ──────────────────────────────── ) × ───
  (1,000 ) 10
  </img>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 22, 2013]

Article 45 (Notification of persons eligible for benefits) When a person becomes eligible for death benefits or disability benefits (hereinafter referred to as "benefits"), the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall, without delay, notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of such fact. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Apr. 11, 2023>

Article 46 (Claim for benefits) (1) Benefits shall be requested to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, but benefits shall not be paid if no request is made within five years from the date of retirement due to death or injury. <Amended on Nov. 10, 2020; Apr. 11, 2023>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), death benefits payable where a person is deemed to have died in the line of duty from the findings of a review by a common review committee or a re-review by the central review committee may be claimed within 5 years from the date on which a decision is made on death in the line of duty. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020>
  (3) Where a person fails to claim benefits within the period prescribed in paragraph (1) or (2) due to wartime, incident, or other similar reasons, the period shall be extended by 2 years. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 10, 2020>

Article 47 (Compensation) (1) Persons eligible for compensation under Article 8(1) of the Act shall be classified as follows:
  1. A person who has retired after having been injured in the course of performing his duties or undergoing education and training directly related to national defense and security or the protection of lives and property of the people and who has been granted a disability rating assigned under Article 6-4 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State: A soldier or a police official wounded in action under Article 4(1)6 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State;
  2. A person who has retired after having been injured in the course of performing his duties or undergoing education and training directly related to national defense and security or the protection of lives and property of the people and who has been granted a disability rating assigned under Article 6 of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation: A soldier or police officer killed in a disaster under Article 2(1)2 of the Act on the Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation;
  3. The bereaved family of a person who died while performing his duties or while performing education and training directly related to the national defense or security or the protection of the lives and property of citizens: The bereaved family of a soldier or police official killed in the line of duty under Article 4(1)5 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State;
  4. The bereaved family of a person who died while performing his duties or while performing education and training directly unrelated to the national defense or security or the protection of the lives and property of citizens: The bereaved family of a soldier or police officer killed in a disaster under Article 2(1)1 of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation;
  (2) A person who intends to receive compensation pursuant to Article 8(1) of the Act shall file an application for registration pursuant to Article 6 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State or Article 4 of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veteran's Compensation.
  (3) Upon receipt of a request from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to verify facts relevant to the requirements for persons who have rendered distinguished service to the State or persons eligible for veteran's compensation, pursuant to Article 9(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Services to the State or Article 6(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veteran's Compensation, the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall confirm such facts and notify the Minister thereof without delay. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Apr. 11, 2023>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 22, 2013]

Article 48 (Restriction on benefits) Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 43 and 44, no benefits shall be paid to persons falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
  1. A person who has been sentenced to imprisonment without prison labor or heavier punishment due to a cause while on service;
  2. A person in whose case a reason to pay benefits has occurred due to his or her intention or gross negligence;
  3. A person who contracts a disease, is injured or dies while leaving without permission.

Article 49 (Medical treatment for the injured) (1) "Medical facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 8(2) of the Act means medical institutions under Article 3 of the Medical Service Act. <Newly Inserted on Jun. 23, 2006>
  (2) The head of a fire service agency shall request the head of a medical institution under paragraph (1) to take medical treatment for an obligatory firefighter who is required to receive medical treatment due to an injury or disease in the course of performing his duties, and the head of the medical institution shall, upon receipt of a request for medical treatment, take appropriate medical treatment according to the degree of injury or disease of the person subject to medical treatment. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>
  (3) When an obligatory firefighter is injured while performing his duties, he may receive first aid at a nearby military medical facility. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>
  (4) Expenses for medical treatment under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall be borne by the State or a local government. <Amended on Jun. 23, 2006>
  (5) When the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency intends to have obligatory firefighter treated in a national medical facility, he or she shall consult with the head of the central administrative agency having jurisdiction over the relevant medical facility in advance on the number of expected medical patients for each medical department for the following year and other necessary matters. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Jun. 23, 2006; Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 50 (Basic supplies expenses) Basic supplies expenses necessary for their daily lives shall be paid to obligatory firefighters within the budget.

Article 51 (Fixed number of members of auxiliary police company) The fixed number of obligatory firefighters shall be determined by the Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency within budgetary limits in consultation with the Minister of National Defense. <Amended on May. 24, 2004; Nov. 19, 2014; Act No. Jul. 26, 2017>

Article 52 (Procedures for complaints) (1) When a commander intends to file a complaint against any obligatory firefighter who violates Article 9 or 10 of the Act pursuant to Article 11(2) of the Act, he shall submit a written complaint to the competent prosecutors' office or its branch office or the competent police station.
  (2) When a commander intends to file a complaint against an obligatory firefighter pursuant to paragraph (1), he shall obtain prior approval from the head of a higher-level fire service agency.
  (3) Where a person violates Article 9 or 10 of the Act, the commander shall take care in determining whether to file a complaint against him, taking into comprehensive consideration his motive for violation, the degree of his penitence, his basic character and conduct, work performance, etc.
  (4) No complaint referred to in paragraph (1) shall be withdrawn.

Article 53 (Management of sensitive information and personally identifiable information) The head of a fire service agency or station may manage data containing information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act and resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act, where it is unavoidable to conduct the following affairs:
  1. Affairs concerning personnel management, including appointment of obligatory firefighters, under the Act and this Decree;
  2. Affairs concerning compensation, including payment of benefits, under the Act and this Decree;
  3. Affairs concerning medical treatment for the injured, etc. referred to in Article 49.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Oct. 22, 2013]
